title: kcdx verification report
description: The frozen cross-repo contract for the in-game verification report. Produced by the in-game kcdx verification test-suite plugin (writes one report file alongside kcdx-dev.log at engine startup, design D28); consumed client-side by the maintainer-tool frontend's verification worklist via the File API (design D31b, no backend read seam). Per-row verdict carries the version-applicability + reachability meaning (design D25), NOT a runtime body hash. The producer emits kcdx_id + resolved version + verdict + detail per row; the consumer resolves the entity name from its own loaded DB by kcdx_id (a kcdx_id absent from the DB is the stale-report case the consumer surfaces).

schema_version.description: The pinned contract version. A consumer rejects a report whose schema_version it does not recognize. Frozen to the value 2 (v1 was the original frozen shape; v2 adds the per-row matched_address_version_id attribution field).

game_version.description: The resolved game/DLL version the report was produced against (design D28 'version stamp'). The version-applicability hash and reachability checks were run on the build that resolved to this version; the consumer shows it in the worklist and matches it against its DB version intervals. A free-form version string in the project's resolved-tag form (e.g. 'release_1_5_1164953_841' or '1.5.1164953').

summary.description: The roll-up the consumer's 'M/N passing' header binds (design D28 + s08). passing = count of rows whose verdict is resolves_works; total = count of rows in the report.

passing.description: Count of rows with verdict resolves_works.

total.description: Count of rows in the report (== rows array length).

rows.description: One entry per DB row the in-game pass checked.

kcdx_id.description: The curated entity id (== the address_names.id the engine plugins reference). The consumer resolves the entity name from its own loaded DB by this id; an id not present in the DB is the stale-report row the consumer flags.

version.description: The resolved address_versions version the row was checked at (the version interval the running build fell into for this entity). Free-form version string in the project's resolved-tag form.

verdict.description: The startup-pass verdict (design D25/D28). EXACTLY these four snake_case tokens are valid report verdicts. resolves_works = on-disk version-applicability hash matches AND the address resolves into live .text. wrong_target = the on-disk hash mismatches (the build diverged from the DB's recorded version) -> avoid applying. dead = the address does not resolve into live .text (unreachable) -> avoid. cannot_check = no content_hash / a non-byte kind / a deferred kind (e.g. vtable_index) -> not checkable this run. Note: 'ambiguous' is an author-time static (s04) outcome, NOT a report verdict -- it is deliberately absent from this enum.

detail.description: A free-text cause string naming what the check observed (the consumer renders it as the per-row detail line). Required and present on every row; the empty string is permitted (e.g. a clean resolves_works row may carry no extra cause).

matched_address_version_id.description: The id of the address_version row whose fingerprint the swept bytes matched (the row attribution). Present on every row; an integer (>= 0) on a resolves_works row, null otherwise. The in-game sweep tries each candidate address_version row's fingerprint (content_hash for a function, the per-kind datum otherwise) and records WHICH row matched; the importer uses this id to extend the matched row's interval forward when the swept version sat in a gap (a passing gap-pass grows that one row's coverage). The attribution invariant: a resolves_works row matched SOME candidate row, so it carries a non-null integer that names which; a wrong_target row matched NO candidate row, and a dead / cannot_check row was not byte-matched at all, so each carries null. A non-pass row never names a matched row; a pass row always does. (The integer-or-null type + the verdict-conditional are enforced by the row-object if/then/else.)
